# Projective Completion and Changed Coordinates

## #0 — Specify which space is completed

Completion changes the representational object under an explicit rule. The [projective line](projective-line.md) adds one point to an affine line over a chosen field; the [Riemann sphere](riemann-sphere.md) gives the complex case its compact surface. The [NIST house](../../episteme/sources/mathematics-logic/nist/nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable/nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable.md) warrants that complex completion, not every projective construction.

The [core's](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) dimensional-reframing operation receives these as exact neighbours. Its native claim is kept distinct from the construction that carries it.

## #1 — Homogenise an affine plane

Embed a real affine point `(x,y)` as `[x:y:1]` in `ℝP²`, whose points are nonzero triples modulo common nonzero scale. The affine line `y=mx+c` becomes `v=mu+cw` in homogeneous coordinates `[u:v:w]`.

For two distinct parallel lines with the same slope `m` and different intercepts, subtracting their homogeneous equations gives `w=0`. Their common projective point is then `[1:m:0]`. Different slopes give different points on the line at infinity.

## #2 — Work a pair of parallels

Take `y=2x+1` and `y=2x−3`. Their affine equations have no common solution. Homogenised, they are `v=2u+w` and `v=2u−3w`. Together they imply `4w=0`, hence `w=0` and `v=2u`. Since the triple is nonzero, the intersection is `[1:2:0]`.

This is an exact intersection in the enlarged projective plane. It does not assert that the original affine lines meet at a finite coordinate, and it does not assign a real scalar to ordinary division by zero.

## #3 — Distinguish homogeneous coordinates from added dimension

The triple has three components, but quotienting by nonzero scale leaves projective dimension 2. Homogenisation uses an extra coordinate; it does not simply raise the intrinsic dimension of the affine plane by one. Similarly `ℂP¹` has complex dimension 1 and real dimension 2.

One-point compactification of the complex plane and projective completion of the real affine plane also have different boundaries: the former adds one point, the latter an entire projective line. Saying merely “infinity becomes a point” would conceal which construction is operating.

## #4 — Preserve the original limit

A changed chart can make a previously unavailable coordinate finite without making every operation globally defined. Reciprocal extends on a projective line; a general binary quotient still has indeterminate cases. A chosen completion has its own topology, transformations and exclusions.

The native interpretation reads this as an account learning to state the limits of its representation and move through them without discarding the achieved determination. The proof of a projective intersection does not independently prove an ontology of unobjectifiable ground. The relation is Argued through the explicit representational change.

## #5→0 — Return with both descriptions available

The result holds the affine failure and projective success together: the lines do not meet in the original plane, and their completed representatives meet at the named ideal point. Neither statement cancels the other because their spaces differ.

This record returns-to [Movement28](../../../section-rooms/04-mathematical-substrate/movements/28-s3-p3-projective-dimensional-reframing.md), [A18](../../../section-rooms/arguments/A18-Primordial-Symbolon-and-Its-Eight-Determinations.md), and [translations](../mono-poly/translations.md). The exact construction remains recoverable beneath the native movement it makes available.
